Does prescribed gain help this example?

One LibriSpeech utterance, one sloping audiogram, stationary white noise. HASPI v2 scores compare no processing with the exact Clarity NAL-R FIR. This is a feasibility check, not evidence of population benefit. The live browser uses a different approximate filter bank.

These files use Clarity’s hearing-loss model offline. Playback applies a shared 0.5 multiplier; it is not calibrated to your headphones. They are not the inputs to the HASPI calculation above.

A fair comparison protocol

  1. Freeze a shared test set with held-out talkers, rooms and listener profiles. Keep calibration, resampling and references identical.
  2. Compare unprocessed, amplification-only, amplification + WDRC, then real multichannel and neural enhancement with identical downstream fitting.
  3. Report hearing-aware intelligibility and quality, binaural cue errors, target distortion, clipping, compute, latency, memory and energy separately.
  4. Run ablations for gain, compression, cue preservation, lookahead and steering errors. Label oracle access explicitly.
  5. Use confidence intervals across independent speakers/listeners. Validate with hearing-impaired listener testing before claiming perceptual benefit.

Edition 0.3 now includes a separate free-field microphone-array DS/MVDR experiment and pretrained RNNoise. Automatic localization, target tracking, measured BTE scenes and a shared downstream fitting evaluation remain next steps.
